draft.title: Improving liveability locally
card: Liveability is how well a place meets the needs of the people who live there. Councils and community groups can both help make a place more liveable.
building and looking after parks, playgrounds and community centres where people meet, relax and join in. Community groups often run activities there.
building footpaths, bike paths and bus shelters. The state government runs most buses and trains, but councils can plan for, and ask for, better links.
planting street trees for shade and cooler streets, and adding better lighting so people feel safer walking at night.
draft.remember: Councils and community groups lift liveability with parks, community centres, paths, transport links, street trees and safer streets.

a.q: Families in a Melbourne suburb say the streets near the station feel unsafe after dark because they are so dim. Which local strategy fits this problem best?
opts: Add better lighting along the streets
Build a new playground in the local park
Add a bike path from homes to the shops
Open a bigger library in the town centre
a.why: The problem is about feeling unsafe in the dark, so better lighting makes the streets safer. A playground, bike path or library could make the suburb more liveable in other ways, but none of them deals with dim streets.
a.clue: Match the problem to the type of local improvement.

b.q: People in a regional Victorian town say they cannot walk safely from their homes to the shops. Which council strategy fits this problem best?
opts: Build a footpath along the main street
Run a new council train line to the shops
Build a community centre near the town hall
Plant shade trees in the town square
b.why: A footpath gives people a safe place to walk, and building footpaths is council work. A train line is tempting, but the state government runs most trains, so a council would not run its own line.
b.clue: Think about what a council can build.

a.best: Add better lighting along the streets

b.best: Build a footpath along the main street
